autostart.hint: A task in the Windows scheduler looks once an hour and opens the panel when it is not there — one panel, holding whichever profiles were open in it. It tells a working panel from a frozen one: an open panel notes the time every minute, and one that has stopped answering is closed and opened again. What it starts is this very install, under your own account.

develop.hint: Both halves of a recording at once: a passive capture of the wire beside a tracer that wraps the client's own Lua. Switch it on, do the thing in the game ONCE, switch it off — then keep the pair with a description of what was done, or throw it away. A capture nobody labelled is a file nobody can read a week later. The tracer's hooks live in the running client, so Stop is asked politely and the panel puts them back if the child does not.
develop.updates.hint: Off, the panel only moves to published releases — tags vX.Y.Z, cut when a batch of work has been proven. On, it moves to the latest state of the branch, unreleased work included: that is what you want while working on the bot, and what nobody else should be running. The setting is for the whole panel, not for this profile — there is one checkout and every profile runs out of it.
develop.web.recording_hint: Both halves at once: a passive capture of the wire beside a tracer over the client's own Lua. Start it, do the thing in the game ONCE, then stop it — what you type when stopping is kept beside the run files as the description. «Delete run» throws the pair away instead.

opt.autoassist_pause_min.hint: The five assists come back once a day; until then there is nothing to look for.
opt.autoassist_poll.hint: How often the auto-assist looks for a finished UR/★ task.
opt.autoassist_star_wait_min.hint: How long a ripening star may hold one of the day's five helps back. 0 — until the task expires or the day resets.
opt.autoassist_sprint_lead_sec.hint: How many seconds before a star matures the sprint starts. Re-reading the alliance list takes about five of them, so the pressing itself begins a little later — leave the margin. A ripe star is taken in under two minutes, and the client knows the moment in advance, so this costs one wake-up per star and not a faster poll. 0 turns the sprint off.
opt.autoassist_sprint_window_sec.hint: How long that fast pressing may last. It bounds the case of a star that never matures because its owner cancelled the task.
opt.autoloot_limit.hint: More than the daily budget makes no difference.
opt.autoloot_pause_min.hint: How long to wait once the day's robberies are gone.
opt.autoloot_poll.hint: How often the capture's checkpoint is re-read.
opt.daemon_port.hint: The panel picks it: one profile, one client, one port. Nothing to keep unique by hand.
opt.debug_send_url.hint: URL the debug-log archive is sent to. Empty — do not send. A stub for now — no transport is wired.
opt.game_exe.hint: The process name that means the game is running. Read off this machine — LW_GAME_EXE names another one.
opt.kick_hold_min.hint: «Logged in on another device» means somebody is playing the account. Nothing touches the client for this long — not the watchdog, not the self-restart, not the timer — and then the ordinary scheme resumes. 0 — restart at once, as before.
opt.launcher.hint: Read off this machine — the ordinary install, or LW_LAUNCHER when the game lives somewhere else.
opt.log_max_lines.hint: How much the log widget keeps. panel.log is never trimmed.
opt.rdp_session: The game runs in another Windows session
opt.rdp_session.hint: Tick this for a second account: its client lives in a Windows session of its own (its own desktop), not on this one. The panel then looks for THAT client, and stops starting or restarting it from here — that would act on this desktop instead. The link port follows the tick — the panel hands out one nobody else uses.
opt.rdp_user.hint: Picked from the accounts of this machine, which Windows itself lists — a login typed with one letter wrong looks configured and never signs in anywhere. The client is looked for among that user's processes, so this is what tells two identically named clients apart.
opt.sniff_ready_timeout.hint: How long to wait for both halves of a recording to report.
opt.trace_filter.hint: Display filter for the panel log ONLY — the recording on disk always keeps every call. A substring of the Lua function name; «SFS» covers the whole wire. Widening it (e.g. «Manager», «Util») only shows more of what is already on disk, but tens of thousands of lines a second can still freeze the panel log — leave it narrow. Empty shows everything.
opt.watchdog: Relaunch the game when it dies
opt.watchdog.hint: Noticing the game process gone, start it again — at most once every 5 minutes.
opt.win_python.hint: It runs the captures, the robberies and the Lua VM itself. Read off this machine — LW_WIN_PYTHON names another one.

rally_fly.max: Skip a banner farther away than (sec, 0 = any distance):
rally_fly.hint: How long a squad may be in the air on its way to the rally's gathering point. The flight is priced by the game's own numbers — the distance from the base to the leader's tile and that squad's march speed — and a banner priced over this is left alone, so the squad stays home for the next one. A squad on a far banner is busy while every near banner arrives. 0 means any distance.

The «monster» daily cap (Settings → Auto Rally) is honoured. A repeat only counts once the game shows the new rally. The buttons beside the box are the levels rallied at most often — one press each. timers.editor.title: Label in the list:
timers.hint: A ticked errand runs itself once its period has passed; the clock survives a restart — an hour that elapsed with the panel shut fires shortly after it opens. Nothing fires with the game closed; a failed run is not counted and is retried; two errands due at the same moment take their turn rather than going together, unless one is marked «at once» — that one runs on a thread of its own and an ordinary errand steps aside for it at its next step. The list belongs to the profile: edit it with the buttons below — «⟳» re-reads the file if you edited it outside.

graphics.hint: The bot reads the game rather than watching it, so nobody has to look at this picture. On «Simplified» the client draws 10 frames a second at the lowest quality in a 640×480 window — measured at a fraction of a percent of the video card, against a quarter of it for a client left alone, and nothing the bot does gets slower. It applies at once, and it applies to THIS profile's client only, so the account playing in the background can be economising while the one you are watching is not. Half of it survives the game restarting and half does not: the window size comes back by itself, the frame rate and the quality do not — so after a crash or a restart, press it again.

errand.arg.radar.claim.hint: Off leaves the board full on purpose: claiming is what scores, so a week's errands claimed on the duel day are worth far more.
errand.arg.radar.duel_day.hint: 1 is Monday, 7 is Sunday. 0 means the errand asks the game which day it is on.
errand.arg.radar.duel_days.hint: The weekdays the radar scores on. Claiming or hoarding is chosen from the game's own day.
errand.arg.radar.forget: Drop the ones it cannot do
errand.arg.star.count.hint: How many warzones one lap walks. Six is about twenty seconds and leaves the client free.
errand.arg.secret.only_ur.hint: The game's own «only UR» filter is put back on before every send, and a send whose selected tasks are not all UR is refused. Turn it off only to send the cheap leftovers too.
errand.arg.secret.keep.hint: How many idle non-UR tasks the refreshing is content to leave.
errand.arg.secret.diamond_cap.hint: The most one mega refresh may cost in diamonds, and the allowance the ordinary refreshes spend against.
errand.arg.secret.dispatch.hint: Send whatever is standing at the end of the run. With «only UR» on, only the UR tasks go out.
errand.arg.heal.portion.hint: 0 — every wounded soldier at once. The hospital treats one batch at a time, so a portion is as much as you want to wait for; the next one goes in as soon as the queue frees.
errand.arg.heal.help.hint: Puts a help request in front of the alliance while the treatment is running, and skips it when one is already standing.
errand.arg.heal.watch.hint: Collects the healed the moment the game itself says the treatment is over, sends the next portion behind it and asks for help again — inside the game, without asking the server anything in between.
errand.arg.trucks.collect: Collect the trucks that came home
errand.arg.trucks.collect.hint: A truck that has landed holds its load until it is taken, and until then it cannot be sent out again — so the run empties the arrivals first and books its next turn for the moment the nearest truck lands.
errand.arg.trucks.one_at_a_time: Send one truck at a time
errand.arg.trucks.one_at_a_time.hint: Only the best truck standing goes out, under the first — strongest — escort, and the run comes back when it is home to send the next one in its place.
errand.arg.trucks.target.hint: An account without the Reindeer Sleigh Ride tech quietly aims at UR instead.
errand.arg.trucks.diamond_cap.hint: The most one rotation may cost in diamonds when the bag of Trade Contracts is short. 0 = no ceiling.
rewards.hint: The client raises a «here is what you were given» window after almost every collect, help or robbery — even when the bot pressed headless and nobody asked for it. A listener inside the client closes those windows and writes down what was in them. It closes ONLY known reward windows; one it does not know is shown here as «not on the list» and left open, so it can be added by hand.
rewards.unknown: a reward window nobody has vouched for: {window} — left open on purpose
rewards.unknown.title: Not on the list — left open
rally_group.cap: Rallies a day for EACH kind
rally_group.cap.hint: One number for the whole group, and it applies to EACH kind in it: 20 means up to 20 rallies on every monster of the group, not 20 shared between them. The line on the tile counts today's joins across the whole group, so it may stand above this number. 0 — no limit.
rally_group.on.hint: One switch for the whole group — written onto every kind in it.

events.arms.hero.hint: On — the run recruits in the tavern up to the phase's top chest, out of recruit tickets only, never diamonds. Off — it reads the phase and books the next border without pressing anything.
events.arms.hire.confirm: Recruiting spends this account's recruit tickets. Hire up to the phase's top chest?
events.arms.no_recipe: No recipe for this phase yet — its spending ceiling has not been agreed.
timers.item.perform_arms_race: Arms Race: play the phase running now
events.arms.drone: Raise rallies in the drone phase
events.arms.drone.hint: On — the run raises rallies until the stamina ceiling beside it is spent or the phase's top chest is reached. It never goes past the day's own rally caps: what those leave is all it gets, and a phase that therefore scores nothing is the right answer.
events.arms.stamina.hint: The most stamina one drone run may spend. 0 raises nothing.
events.arms.speedup: Spend speed-ups in the building, unit and research phases
events.arms.speedup.hint: On — a run pours speed-ups into the longest queue of the right kind until the phase's top chest is reached or the minute ceiling beside this is spent. Specialised speed-ups go before universal ones, and diamonds are never spent. Off — a run reads the phase and books its border without pressing anything.
events.arms.minutes.hint: A safety limit, not a target: what a phase needs is worked out every run from its own top-chest threshold and from the rate the run measures on its first speed-up. This only says «whatever you worked out, spend no more than this». 0 spends nothing. The log prints what was wanted beside what was spent. Small speed-ups go before large ones, and specialised before universal.
events.arms.units: Train soldiers in the unit phase
events.arms.units.hint: On — a run collects every barracks that has finished its batch and starts the biggest new one each free barracks will take, up to the soldier ceiling beside this. What it spends is the base's own resources rather than items from the bag, which is why it is a switch of its own. Off — a run reads the phase and books its border without pressing anything.
events.arms.soldiers.hint: The most soldiers one unit-phase run may put into training, over all barracks together. 0 means whatever the barracks themselves accept: each is asked for the size the game has already accepted for it. A live run put 1000 in and scored 28000 of that phase's 75000.
events.arms.free_minutes.hint: How many minutes of speed-up a unit-phase run may spend to empty a barracks that is still training, so a new scoring batch can start in it. Not the fuse above: that one buys points in the building and research phases, this one buys an empty barracks. 0 trains only into barracks that are already free. Soldier speed-ups go before universal ones, small pieces before large, and diamonds are never spent.
events.arms.train.confirm: Start a batch in every free barracks? It spends the base's own resources, up to the soldier ceiling.
events.arms.spend.confirm: This spends this account's own speed-ups into a queue. Spend up to the minute ceiling?
events.arms.raise.confirm: Raising sends the squad out of the base and spends this day's rallies and stamina. Raise up to the ceiling?

errand.arg.heal.chests.hint: When the base cannot pay for the treatment, opens exactly the resource packs the game itself picks to cover what is missing — and no more. Off: the run still says what the treatment costs and what is short.
